bites.title: Genes, diseases, and drugs as nodes and edges
bites.body:
A biomedical knowledge graph organises biological facts into a structured network where entities such as genes, proteins, pathways, diseases, and drugs are represented as nodes, and the relationships between them (such as "inhibits", "causes", or "treats") are represented as typed, directed edges.

It is like a detective's investigation board where photos of people, companies, and locations are linked by labelled strings showing who paid or met whom.

Unlike unstructured text paragraphs, a knowledge graph makes relationships explicit and machine-queryable across millions of facts integrated from curated databases and literature. However, a graph is only as clean as its ingestion pipeline; poorly normalised nodes create duplicate islands that break graph traversal.
bites.sourceNote: Drafted by AI, November 2026 · confidence: high

questions.prompt: How does a biomedical knowledge graph represent scientific knowledge differently from raw journal text?

choices.text: It stores every research paper as an unindexed MP3 audio recording of the author reading aloud
It deletes all information about chemical drugs and retains only patient billing postcodes
It structures entities like genes, drugs, and diseases as nodes connected by explicitly typed relationship edges
It replaces specific relationship types with unlabelled random connections between words

questions.explanation: Knowledge graphs turn unstructured assertions into explicit subject-predicate-object triples that algorithms and scientists can traverse systematically.

bites.title: Multi-hop queries (gene to pathway to drug)
bites.body:
A multi-hop query traverses a chain of connected nodes and edges across a knowledge graph to answer questions that no single document states in one place. For example, a researcher might trace from a disease-associated gene to the biological pathway it regulates, to a partner protein in that pathway, and finally to an approved drug that inhibits that partner.

It is like finding a flight connection from a small regional town to another continent by routing through two major hub airports.

The practical risk is combinatorial explosion: after three or four hops through hub nodes like inflammation or ATP, thousands of noisy, trivial paths appear. Consultants must constrain multi-hop searches by edge type, tissue specificity, and evidence confidence.
bites.sourceNote: Drafted by AI, November 2026 · confidence: high

questions.prompt: What is the main danger of running unconstrained multi-hop queries across four or five steps in a biomedical knowledge graph?

choices.text: Graph databases refuse to execute any query that crosses more than one edge type
Traversing through high-degree hub nodes creates a combinatorial explosion of noisy, biologically trivial paths
Multi-hop queries permanently delete the nodes they visit from the underlying storage engine
Connecting a gene to a pathway automatically invalidates the drug's chemical structure

questions.explanation: Without filtering by edge type and confidence, multi-hop paths rapidly fan out through generic hub nodes and return thousands of meaningless associations.

bites.title: Graph RAG over biomedical knowledge
bites.body:
Graph RAG combines vector-based text retrieval with structured traversal of a biomedical knowledge graph to answer complex scientific questions. When a user asks how a drug might affect a disease, the system retrieves both relevant literature passages and the structured subgraph of genes, pathways, and interactions linking the two entities.

It is like preparing a strategy brief using both detailed witness interview transcripts and an accountant's structured spreadsheet of company transfers.

Graph RAG excels at multi-entity synthesis and structured completeness where chunk-based text RAG misses connections spread across separate papers. The trade-off is higher engineering cost to maintain entity linking and ontology alignment; consultants should deploy Graph RAG when multi-hop relational reasoning truly justifies the complexity.
bites.sourceNote: Drafted by AI, November 2026 · confidence: high

questions.prompt: How does Graph RAG complement standard text-chunk RAG in biomedical discovery workflows?

choices.text: It pairs structured multi-hop entity relationships from a knowledge graph with detailed textual evidence from literature passages
It eliminates the need to store any source text or citations by memorising only node colours
It runs exclusively on analogue hardware without requiring any database indexing
It restricts user queries to single-word lookups of chemical molecular weights

questions.explanation: Graph RAG uses structured graph topology to find multi-step biological connections while grounding each link in retrieved text passages.

bites.title: Standard identifiers and ontologies connect the sources
bites.body:
Integrating twenty biomedical databases into one knowledge graph requires standard identifiers and formal ontologies such as Ensembl or Entrez for genes, UniProt for proteins, ChEMBL or DrugBank for compounds, and Mondo or EFO for diseases. Because ontology mappings update continuously, check the current details and release versions when building ETL pipelines.

It is like international shipping using universal barcode and customs codes so ports in every country recognise the exact same cargo container.

Without strict ontology alignment, "breast carcinoma" in one dataset and "malignant neoplasm of breast" in another remain disconnected nodes. AI consultants should treat identifier mapping and cross-reference governance as the foundational step of any biomedical data platform.
bites.sourceNote: Drafted by AI, November 2026 · fast-moving topic, check current details · confidence: medium

questions.prompt: Why are standard ontologies and identifiers (such as UniProt, Ensembl, and Mondo) essential when building a biomedical knowledge graph?

choices.text: They encrypt the database so that scientists cannot read the names of human chromosomes
They compress gigapixel pathology images into three-letter amino acid codes
They allow any laboratory to invent private, unmapped names for common generic medicines
They align disparate databases onto shared canonical concepts so identical genes or diseases are not split into duplicate nodes

questions.explanation: Canonical identifiers and hierarchical ontologies unify naming differences across sources, enabling clean data integration and hierarchical reasoning.

bites.title: Evidence on each edge: source, type, and strength
bites.body:
In a rigorous biomedical knowledge graph, an edge connecting a gene to a disease is never just a bare line; it carries rich provenance metadata recording the source database or paper, the experimental evidence type (such as human genetic association, CRISPR screen, or text mining), and a confidence or statistical strength score.

It is like a bridge registry that records whether each river crossing is a reinforced motorway viaduct, a wooden footbridge, or an unverified rumour.

An edge extracted automatically by an NLP script from an abstract sentence is far weaker than a curated clinical trial outcome or human loss-of-function genetics. Consultants must ensure agents and UIs filter and weight graph edges by provenance and evidence tier.
bites.sourceNote: Drafted by AI, November 2026 · confidence: high

questions.prompt: Why should every edge in a biomedical knowledge graph store provenance, evidence type, and confidence metadata?

choices.text: Graph visualisation software cannot draw a line on screen unless it contains at least fifty metadata fields
Provenance metadata automatically converts mouse cell-line experiments into approved human therapies
It lets users and agents distinguish high-confidence human genetic or clinical evidence from weak text-mined associations
Storing source identifiers reduces the number of nodes in the graph to zero

questions.explanation: Recording how a relationship was discovered and how strong the support is prevents weak or noisy assertions from polluting downstream reasoning.

bites.title: Graph links are hypotheses to check, not facts
bites.body:
When a knowledge graph or link-prediction model surfaces a novel connection between a target gene and a patient indication, that link represents a structured scientific hypothesis rather than an established biological fact. Literature-mined edges can reflect negated sentences, speculate in discussion sections, or hold true only in artificial cell lines.

It is like a market analyst spotting a correlation between two retail trends: it tells you where to investigate next, not that a merger is guaranteed to succeed.

Even curated database edges are often context-dependent and lack tissue directionality. Train client teams to use knowledge graph paths as a hypothesis-ranking engine that always leads into primary source inspection and experimental validation.
bites.sourceNote: Drafted by AI, November 2026 · confidence: high

questions.prompt: How should drug-discovery teams treat novel target-disease links surfaced by a biomedical knowledge graph?

choices.text: As prioritised hypotheses that require verification in primary literature and wet-lab experiments
As proven causal mechanisms ready to advance directly into human clinical dosing
As mathematical errors that must be deleted whenever they are not already famous
As regulatory approvals issued automatically by national medicines agencies

questions.explanation: Graph links aggregate noisy, context-specific observations and predictions, making them valuable starting points for investigation rather than final proof.
